description:
FILED s446l (agent L) from #502 probes; PRE-EXISTING.

REPRO: a file containing `print "[$0]\n";` -- perl prints the script's path,
PCL prints `sbcl`.  Cause: cl/pcl-runtime.lisp:999
    (defvar $0 (or (car sb-ext:*posix-argv*) "perl") "Program name")
which is the SBCL binary, because the emitted CL is loaded BY sbcl.  Nothing
later sets it from the perl source file.

This makes $0 (and English's $PROGRAM_NAME, which aliases it) wrong for every
program, and it is the value real scripts use for usage messages, re-exec, and
`basename $0` logging.  It is also SILENT: the program keeps running.

FIX SHAPE: the transpiler already knows the source path (it writes
`(setf pcl::*pcl-pl2cl-path* ...)` into the preamble), so the preamble can set
$0 to the .pl file's path the same way -- one emitted form, keyed on the input
file, with STDIN input keeping the current answer (perl's `-` for a piped
script).  Check the interactions first: `pl2cl --module` must NOT set it (a
module load would clobber the program's $0); tools/pclperl-for-tests and the
sweep spawn children whose $0 the harness may compare; perl-tests/t/test.pl
and the fresh_perl machinery are the places to look.  ALSO: perl lets $0 be
WRITTEN (it rewrites the process title) -- decide whether the write is a no-op
that keeps the value (probe what a write then read gives in perl).

BAR: $0 read from a file / from STDIN / inside a required module / after a
write; $PROGRAM_NAME through lib/English.pm; a full sweep (cl/ + emission).


s445 (Fable): CLOSED AS DUPLICATE of #512, which agent I shipped this round -- probed on the merged tree (8600556): $0 is the script path and matches perl byte for byte; the write-through-handle consequence works too. #571 ($^E/$^C) verified STILL OPEN on the same tree.
subject: $0 is `sbcl`, not the script path -- `(defvar $0 (car sb-ext:*posix-argv*))` reports the HOST binary
